key_idea: Use blow-up limits of the measure to get flat reflectionless limits. Normal heights renormalized by the excess satisfy a nonlocal (half-Laplacian-type) equation in the limit, and its Liouville-type affine rigidity yields relative excess decay at every scale, which propagates flatness into uniform rectifiability.
reason: There is a recognizable, reasonably conceptual core: a compactness-plus-linearization excess-improvement scheme in which the renormalized height solves a fractional Laplace equation and so must be affine. Around it sit a long chain of technical lemmas (Bessel packing, Carleson families, annular alternatives, moving-measure energy compactness, polarization, plane comparisons) carrying heavy bookkeeping. That buries the idea and makes the structure hard to hold in one's head.
recognized: A proof that L^2-boundedness of the n-dimensional Riesz transform implies uniform rectifiability (the David–Semmes problem) for 2≤n≤d−2, in the style of the Nazarov–Tolsa–Volberg approach with Mas–Tolsa variational consequences; I don't recognize this specific text
